tylodorhynchus:study:1.title: A taxonomic note on a coloborhynchine pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation:  Tylodorhynchus rodriguesae gen. et comb. nov  . (Historical Biology, 2026)

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Tylodorhynchus was discovered in 2014 by Will Thurbin at Sudmour Point on the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight, England.
facts.quote: The only known Tylodorhynchus specimen was discovered in 2014 by Will Thurbin at Sudmour Point southwest coast of the Isle of Wight, England

facts.statement: The specimen was donated to the Dinosaur Isle museum and assigned the catalog number IWCMS 2014.82.
facts.quote: The specimen was subsequently donated to the Dinosaur Isle museum by Thurbin and given the specimen number IWCMS 2014.82

facts.statement: Pêgas and Holgado published a reassessment of the specimen in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Pêgas and Holgado published a study based on a reassessment of IWCMS 2014.82

facts.statement: The genus name Tylodorhynchus combines Greek words for "callused" and "beak" to describe a callus-like projection on the palate.
facts.quote: They assigned it to a new genus, Tylodorhynchus, combining the Ancient Greek words τυλώδης (tylōdēs, "callused") and ῥύγχος (rhynchos, "beak") based on the callus-like projection on the palate

facts.statement: Tylodorhynchus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian stage.
Tylodorhynchus is classified as a coloborhynchine anhanguerid and was established as a new genus for the species formerly known as Uktenadactylus rodriguesae.
facts.quote: A coloborhynchine anhanguerid; a new genus for "Uktenadactylus" rodriguesae Holgado & Pêgas (2020)

facts.statement: The genus Tylodorhynchus was described by Pêgas and Holgado in 2026.
The species was reassigned to the new genus Tylodorhynchus because it differed from Uktenadactylus wadleighi, which was found to be more closely related to Nicorhynchus.
facts.quote: Therefore, they assigned it to a new genus, Tylodorhynchus

facts.statement: As a coloborhynchine, Tylodorhynchus had a boxy snout ending in a flat, blunt front surface called the deltoid facet.
facts.quote: As a member of the subfamily Coloborhynchinae, the end of this snout was boxy in shape, and the upper jaw ended in a flat, blunt front surface known as the deltoid facet

facts.statement: The preserved front base of the crest has a flat top margin, unlike the grooved surface found in Uktenadactylus and Nicorhynchus.
facts.quote: Only the front base of the crest is preserved, but it has a flat surface along its top margin unlike the grooved surface seen in Uktenadactylus and Nicorhynchus

facts.statement: A small blunt protrusion at the base of the crest is unique to Tylodorhynchus among anhanguerids.
facts.quote: At the base of the crest (at the top of the deltoid facet), there is a small blunt protrusion not seen in any other species of anhanguerid

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the bulbous projection on Uktenadactylus wadleighi may be a pathology rather than a typical anatomical feature.
facts.quote: Additionally, it was found the bulbous projection on U. wadleighi may be due to a pathology rather than representing the typical anatomy of the animal

facts.statement: Initial assessments suggested that slight differences from Coloborhynchus clavirostris were not sufficient to warrant a distinct species status.
facts.quote: Though slight differences were apparent from the type species Coloborhynchus clavirostris, they were not considered sufficient to establish a distinct species

rejected.quote: Tylodorhynchus is an extinct genus of anhanguerid pterosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian stage) Wessex Formation on the Isle of Wight, England
